title: Normalize caller-owned options without writing results back into them
applies_when: A public connection, table-creation or cache-load API normalizes caller-owned options, storage maps, typed overrides or serialized timestamps, including frozen inputs and repeated reuse; or an HTTP transport injects headers into a caller-owned request.
lesson: A functional normalization helper does not make its caller non-mutating: assigning its returned map to an aliased options object still changes caller state. Trace both the outer object and nested map. Build a local normalized options object, and merge overrides into a local map when that merge would mutate the input. Test frozen outer options with and without a nested map, frozen nested maps, and repeated real API calls that preserve input contents and identity. Retain an already-copying overload as a passing control so the regression isolates the ownership violation. Exercise the native operation after normalization rather than testing a copied expression alone. For Go RoundTripper header injection, WithContext is only a shallow request copy: sequential calls can retain a previous conversation header through the shared map. Clone the request before setting headers, preserve outbound injection, and test an explicitly empty context override after closing each response. Also mutate an outbound header value slice to check that the original values no longer alias it. When importing cache snapshots, convert portable wall-clock timestamps into local clock values without writing the conversion back into reusable entries. Test a second cache and a second load of the same snapshot, with no-TTL and separately serialized inputs as controls. A spread copies only enumerable own properties: read declared Entry fields directly if inherited getters are supported.
avoid_when: An explicitly documented in-place builder may own and modify its input. A visible pop/update may target a returned copy: vLLM Humming copies resolved layer options and compressed input groups before popping allow_fallback. Check the actual helper and base/override values across calls; this does not prove nested mutable values or every configuration write isolated. Do not confuse caller-input preservation with equality between raw payload and a canonical request: a constructor can intentionally normalize aliases or materialize iterators. Snapshot each relevant boundary separately and compare it before/after the operation under test. vLLM renames reasoning_content to reasoning before request field validation; comparing that canonical object directly to the old payload invents a failure unrelated to subsequent tokenizer behavior. This is not proof that all constructor mutation is intended or harmless. A shallow object spread does not isolate later writes to nested objects; copy the specific nested map where needed, not every object or opaque handle. Go Request.Clone does not deep-copy Body, and RoundTripper is allowed to consume and close it; do not generalize header isolation into body ownership changes or test concurrent request reuse as if supported. Preserving caller input does not prove option precedence, native lifetime, concurrency, all overloads or performance. Released native libraries do not establish current-head native-build compatibility, and an open PR or fork branch is not a merged fix.

evidence.note: resolve_humming_layer_config copies the base dict and updates the copy with a matching dynamic override. This protects top-level removal, not arbitrary mutation of nested values.

compressed_tensors_get_config copies a selected input group before returning it. Inspect this alias boundary before attributing the later allow_fallback pop to checkpoint corruption; not GPU/model or cache-lifecycle qualification.

ChatCompletionRequest._normalize_messages_before explicitly renames the deprecated reasoning_content alias to reasoning and materializes tool-call iterators before union validation. This supports checking canonicalization separately from later input preservation; it does not establish a general no-mutation guarantee, HTTP behavior or model correctness.

Exact proposed connection fix copies the outer options before assigning the normalized storage map; URI and namespace entry points previously aliased caller options, while the object overload already copied them.

Public native-database regressions cover frozen and reused inputs. Contributor reproduction reports six affected entry-point failures and three unchanged overload controls before the entry fix, then 52 passing tests afterward.

Open correctness PR also keeps table-creation storage merges local and preserves typed option precedence. Validation uses current TypeScript with a released native library plus strict matching-release checks; no current-head Rust/native rebuild, GPU or performance claim.

Pinned upstream transport injects provider and conversation headers directly into the caller's request. This implementation path lets the existing source-affinity reader find the scoped ownership lesson; the source link alone is not a runtime or production-prevalence result.

The documented transport contract preserves request fields except consuming/closing Body; callers wait until the response Body is closed before reuse. Request.WithContext is shallow while Request.Clone deep-copies headers but not Body. Mechanism, not a security or performance claim.

Contributor-native Linux amd64 Go1.27.2 validation of actual goraven/util and real pinned modules: original b176662 source plus identical focused tests gives 2 regression failures and 3 passes; the one-line Request.Clone repair gives 5 passes. Full util ordinary/race each gives 59 passing test/subtest events, no failures/skips, and vet/gofmt pass. Source and go.mod/go.sum postchecks match frozen bytes. Not whole application, debug-mode coverage, Windows/minimum-Go/CI, security impact, performance, maintainer acceptance or prospective selector benefit.

Pinned load contract accepts portable Date.now start values, then overwrites entry.start with the cache clock conversion. Reusing that same entry causes another conversion; this source mechanism motivates repeated-load tests, not a general TTL guarantee or a published/merged repair claim. Entry's four declared fields are at lines1188-1193.
